## Goal
Harden the pure reply matcher in `src/freemyid/engine/mail.py` (`scan_replies`, lines 216-260) without changing what it returns for normal broker mail.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
- `sender_domain` (`mail.py:149-154`) takes the domain from the From header's real address (`email.utils.getaddresses` or the policy's parsed address), not the first `@` in the header. A From like `"privacy@broker.example" <x@attacker.example>` must give `attacker.example`, so `check_sender` rejects it and its links are never used.
- `_EXTENSION` (`mail.py:60-64`) no longer matches a bare "extension" (a phone extension or browser extension in a footer). It needs a time word near it, as the security review asked (`docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md` line 687, INFO). Table-driven cases: "we are taking a 45-day extension" and "we need additional time" match; "call us at ext. 204", "phone extension 12" and "install our browser extension" don't.
- `claims_extension` applies the same `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` cap as `asks_for_id` (`mail.py:204-213`).
- Each message is parsed once per `scan_replies` call (today `sender_domain`, `_message_key`, `message_date`, `asks_for_id` and `claims_extension` each re-parse it). A test with a counting fake parser or a timing-free call count proves it.
- `ReplyScan` fields and order are unchanged; read `tests/codex/test_cx_reply_matcher_fuzz.py` and `tests/test_mail_sec50_53.py` first and keep them passing.
